concept.title: Acintyabhedābheda
concept.description: The Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava doctrine of acintyabhedābheda (inconceivable simultaneous oneness and difference), associated with Jīva Gosvāmī, stating that the relationship between Kṛṣṇa and his potencies is beyond logical categorization; its epistemological and theological implications are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.description: In Advaita Vedānta, adhyāsa (superimposition) is the erroneous attribution of the qualities of the non-self (anatman) to the self (ātman); its definition, types (svarūpa and samsarga), and role in bondage are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.description: The Advaita doctrine of ajāti-vāda (non-origination), associated with Gauḍapāda, asserting that the world of birth and death never truly originates and that Brahman alone is real; its arguments and relation to Māṇḍūkya Kārikā are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.description: The Āgamic (Tantric) tradition: the Śaiva Āgamas (28 principal texts), Vaiṣṇava Pāñcarātras and Vaikhānasas, Śākta Tantras; their structure (jñāna, yoga, kriyā, caryā), their role in temple ritual, iconography, and initiation (dīkṣā); their distinction from Vedic orthopraxy and their integration into Smārta tradition are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Bhagavad Gītā Philosophy

concept.description: The Bhāgavata Purāṇa (Śrīmad Bhāgavatam), its twelve skandhas, focus on Kṛṣṇa-bhakti, the daśāvatāra, and the dialogue between Parīkṣit and Śuka; its theological emphasis on bhakti-yoga is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Bhakti Movement
concept.description: The Bhakti movement (7th–17th centuries): the devotional renaissance across India emphasizing personal devotion (bhakti) to a chosen deity (iṣṭa-devatā) over ritual orthodoxy; its poet-saints (Āḻvārs, Nāyanārs, Vārkarīs, Haridāsas, Rāmānanda, Kabīr, Tulsīdās, Mīrābāī, Sūrdās, Caitanya); its vernacular literature, social egalitarianism, and lasting impact on Hindu practice are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Sāṃkhya Evolution (Parinama)
concept.description: The Sāṃkhya theory of cosmic evolution (pariṇāma) from prakṛti: the sequential manifestation of mahat (buddhi), ahaṃkāra (ego), the five tanmātras (subtle elements), the five mahābhūtas (gross elements), the five jñānendriyas (sense organs), the five karmendriyas (action organs), and manas (mind); the teleological direction of evolution toward the liberation of puruṣa is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Vaiśeṣika Atomism
concept.description: The Vaiśeṣika atomic theory positing four kinds of eternal, indivisible atoms (paramāṇu) — earth, water, fire, air — each with distinct qualities (guṇa); their binary combinations (dvyanuka) and ternary combinations (tryanuka) forming the gross physical world; the theory's differences from Greek atomism and its role in Vaiśeṣika physics are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

concept.title: Vaiśeṣika Creation Theory

festival.title: Rakṣābandhana
festival.description: Rakṣābandhana (Rakhi), the festival of the protective bond between siblings, observed on the full moon of Śrāvaṇa (Aug); the sister ties a rakhi (sacred thread) on the brother's wrist, and the brother vows protection; its regional variations, historical narratives (Roxana-Poross, Draupadī-Kṛṣṇa), and contemporary practice are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

teacher.title: Annamācārya
teacher.description: Annamācārya (1408–1503), the earliest known composer of saṅkīrtana (devotional songs) in Telugu, dedicated to Veṅkaṭeśvara of Tirumala; his 32,000+ compositions (saṅkīrtanas) on copper plates recovered in the 20th century, his role in the Śrīvaiṣṇava tradition, and his influence on Carnatic music are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

teacher.title: Appayya Dīkṣita
teacher.description: Appayya Dīkṣita (1520–1593), the Advaita Vedānta scholar and Śaiva devotee, author of over 100 works including the Siddhānta-leśa-saṅgraha, Śivārkamaṇi-dīpikā, and Khaṇḍana-khaṇḍa-khādya; his synthesis of Advaita and Śaiva Siddhānta, his debate with Vijayeन्द्र Tīrtha, and his role in the Śrīvidyā tradition are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

teacher.title: Kabīr
teacher.description: Kabīr (c. 1440–1518), the mystic poet-saint of the Bhakti movement, synthesizing Hindu and Islamic devotional traditions; his verses (bījak, sākhīs, śabdas) emphasizing nirguṇa-bhakti (devotion to the formless), the guru, and the critique of ritual orthodoxy; his influence on the Kabīr Panth and Sikh scripture (Gurū Granth Sāhib) is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

teacher.title: Kanakadāsa
teacher.description: Kanakadāsa (1509–1609), the Haridāsa saint-poet from Karnataka, composer of kīrtanas in Kannada dedicated to Adikeshava (Viṣṇu); his works (Mohanatarangini, Ramadhanya Charitre, Nalacharitre) emphasizing bhakti, social equality, and devotion over caste; his association with Udupi and the Krishna temple are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

teacher.title: Muttusvāmi Dīkṣitar
teacher.description: Muttusvāmi Dīkṣitar (1775–1835), one of the Carnatic trinity, composer of ~500 kṛtis in Sanskrit, known for his mastery of rāga, the navagraha kṛtis, the kamalamba navavarṇa kṛtis, and his use of Sanskrit sahitya with intricate rāga structures; his influence on Carnatic music theory is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

teacher.title: Nīlakaṇṭha Dīkṣita
teacher.description: Nīlakaṇṭha Dīkṣita (1613–1697), the Advaita Vedānta scholar and poet, grandson of Appayya Dīkṣita; author of the Śiva-leśa, Śivalīlārṇava, and the satirical Kaliviḍambana; his role in the Śrīvidyā and Advaita traditions in South India is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

teacher.title: Purandaradāsa
teacher.description: Purandaradāsa (1484–1564), the 'father of Carnatic music' (Karnataka Sangeeta Pitamaha), composer of 475,000+ kīrtanas in Kannada and Sanskrit; his systematization of music pedagogy (sarali, janta, alankara, geetam, swarajati, varnam), his devotion to Viṭṭhala, and his role in the Haridāsa movement are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

teacher.title: Rāghavendra Svāmī
teacher.description: Rāghavendra Svāmī (1595–1671), the Dvaita Vedānta pontiff (Rāghavendra Maṭha, Mantralayam), known for his commentaries on Madhva's works and his reputation as a miracle-worker; his role in the Dvaita tradition, the Brindavan at Mantralayam, and his continued popular veneration are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

teacher.title: Rāmakṛṣṇa Paramahaṃsa
teacher.description: Rāmakṛṣṇa Paramahaṃsa (1836–1886), the 19th-century mystic of Dakṣiṇeśvar, devotee of Kālī, who experienced diverse religious paths (Śākta, Vaiṣṇava, Advaita, Islam, Christianity) and declared 'yato mat tato patha' (as many paths, so many ways); his disciple Vivekananda, the Ramakrishna Mission, and his universalist message are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

teacher.title: Rāmānanda
teacher.description: Rāmānanda (c. 14th–15th century), the founder of the Rāmānandī sect, a North Indian Vaiṣṇava tradition emphasizing Rāma-bhakti and the accessibility of devotion regardless of caste; his disciples included Kabīr, Ravidās, and Sena; his role in the Bhakti movement in North India is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

teacher.title: Śyāma Śāstri
teacher.description: Śyāma Śāstri (1762–1827), one of the Carnatic trinity, composer of ~300 kṛtis in Telugu and Sanskrit, known for his swarajatis, his kamakshi navaratna mālikā, his ananda bhairavi compositions, and his distinctive rhythmic structures (tāḷa); his influence on Carnatic music is represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

teacher.title: Śrī Aurobindo
teacher.description: Śrī Aurobindo (1872–1950), the nationalist, philosopher, and yogi who developed Integral Yoga (Pūrṇa Yoga); his works (The Life Divine, Synthesis of Yoga, Savitri), his concept of the Supermind, the descent of consciousness, the Ashram at Pondicherry, and the Auroville township are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

teacher.title: Sūrdās
teacher.description: Sūrdās (c. 1478–1583), the blind poet-saint of the Puṣṭimārga (Vallabha sect), composer of the Sūrsāgar (thousands of Braj bhāṣā poems on Kṛṣṇa-līlā); his depiction of Kṛṣṇa's childhood (bāla-līlā), the gopīs' love, and the philosophy of puṣṭi (grace) are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---

teacher.title: Tulsīdās
teacher.description: Tulsīdās (1532–1623), the composer of the Rāmacaritamānasa (Awadhi retelling of the Rāmāyaṇa), the Hanumān Cālīsā, and the Vinaya Patrikā; his role in popularizing Rāma-bhakti in North India, his founding of the Sankat Mochan Temple (Varanasi), and his influence on the Rāmānandī tradition are represented here as a catalogue entry. ---
